A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Swedish forest landscape is a complex, contested space in which a variety of interests, claims and expectations are negotiated and managed.

the Swedish landscape is not only a site where people and wildlife interact and compete for resources, but also a place for people to interact with one another and negotiate the use of natural resources and the meaning of wildlife.

the Swedish forest is not only an object of governance and management but also an arena for social and political processes that are not necessarily in line with the formalised and regulated management arrangements.
